overview: The United States is a large country in North America made up of 50 states. Its capital is Washington, D.C., and its largest city is New York. The United States declared independence from Britain in 1776. It has the largest economy in the world and is one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council.

geography.text: The mainland United States stretches from the Atlantic to the Pacific. The Appalachian Mountains run down the east, the Great Plains cover the centre and the Rocky Mountains rise in the west. The Mississippi is its main river system, and the Great Lakes lie along the border with Canada. Alaska, in the far north-west, and Hawaii, in the middle of the Pacific, are also states.

history.text: Indigenous peoples had lived in North America for thousands of years before European settlers arrived. Thirteen British colonies declared independence in 1776 and won it in the American Revolution. The country expanded westwards, fought a civil war from 1861 to 1865 that ended slavery, and in the 1900s became a world superpower. The civil rights movement of the 1950s and 1960s fought for equal rights for Black Americans.

events.title: Declaration of Independence
events.text: Thirteen colonies declare independence from Britain.

events.title: Civil War
events.text: Southern states break away; four years of war follow.

events.title: Pearl Harbor
events.text: Japan attacks the US fleet in Hawaii, bringing the US into the Second World War.

events.title: Civil Rights Act
events.text: A law bans discrimination based on race.

events.title: Moon landing
events.text: Apollo 11 astronauts walk on the Moon.

government.text: The United States is a federal republic of 50 states. The President, elected every four years for a maximum of two terms, is both head of state and head of government. Congress has two houses, the House of Representatives and the Senate, and the Supreme Court can strike down laws that break the Constitution, which dates from 1787. Each state has its own government and laws.

economy.text: The United States has the largest economy in the world. It leads in technology, finance, entertainment, medicine and higher education, with companies such as Apple, Microsoft, Google and Amazon. It is also the world's largest producer of oil and natural gas and a huge farm exporter. The US dollar is the main currency of world trade.

culture.text: American films, music, television, video games and fast food are known all over the world. Jazz, blues, rock and roll and hip hop all began in the United States. It is a country of immigrants, with people whose families came from every part of the world, as well as Native American nations.

items.title: Hollywood
items.text: The centre of the US film industry since the 1910s.

items.title: Jazz
items.text: Born in New Orleans in the early 1900s.

items.title: National parks
items.text: Yellowstone, created in 1872, was the world's first national park.

sport.text: Americans follow American football, basketball and baseball most closely, and the Super Bowl is the biggest TV event of the year. The US has won more Olympic medals than any other country, and its women's football team has won the World Cup four times. It co-hosted the 2026 men's World Cup, and Los Angeles will host the 2028 Olympics.

items.title: Olympics
items.text: More Summer Olympic medals than any other country.
Los Angeles hosts the Summer Olympics for the third time.

didYouKnow: The United States has 63 national parks, from Yellowstone, the world's first, to the Gateway Arch.
Alaska was bought from Russia in 1867 for 7.2 million dollars.
